DEVIATION FROM THE CARD. The card says family 'ros', helper RosDriver and role 'sim-env', but the pinned tree has no ROS node, service, action or simulator that carries the primary interface. core/action_interface.py:32 defines ActionInterface; it subscribes only to the two AprilTag observation topics top_camera/tag_detections and wrist_camera/tag_detections (core/action_interface.py:40-49) and drives the arm through direct Python calls on an external PandaArmInterface object (import at :16, construction at :56). Its motion methods are Python methods such as pickup_beam (:97), move_to_input_area (:130), move_beam_to_approach_pose (:170), move_to_beam (:203) and insert_peg (:262). CMakeLists.txt declares no messages, services or actions (catkin_python_setup and generate_messages are commented at :19 and :67; no add_service_files or add_action_files), and launch/bringup_interface.launch only includes external realsense, apriltag_ros and panda_moveit_config launches (:7-31). RosDriver can therefore observe the marker topics but cannot invoke the primary motion, and an observation-only driver would violate the primary-control rule. The matching shape is a direct Driver over this Python object, not RosDriver; that is the card deviation.

WHY NO HONEST STOP EXISTS. The pinned clone defines no stop or e-stop method, service, action or physical e-stop line. The only related calls are recover_from_errors() at core/action_interface.py:371, :657, :815 and :836, whose implementation is in the external panda_interface package and which the clone does not document as a stop, and put_down() at :649-661, which opens the gripper (:658) and commands further upward motion (:659-660); it is a controlled release, not a stop. The comment at :333 is only a loop break. A zero-delta command in exec_pose_delta_cmd (:675-689) is a new impedance command, not fresh stopped-state evidence, and the blocking insertion loops (:305-356, :361-369) have no cancellation check; the inner while not hit_bottom at :307 has no bound, and the outer while not inserted reaches its trials break at :356 only after that inner loop returns. The Franka hardware e-stop is not in this clone, so estop_physical_ref has no source line here; a model must not invent one. The native API cannot enforce the stop, so neither an @estop nor a safe_state action can be honestly declared. A hardware @estop calling a Python method that is not in the clone would also be unsourced. This is the same concrete blocker recorded for other no-native-stop packages.

ADDITIONAL SHIPPED DEFECTS. The concrete entry cannot run as shipped: get_beam_id uses the undefined name target at core/action_interface.py:925; insert_peg calls the undefined name pring at :320; main.py:13 reads assembly before assignment; the planner submodule declared at .gitmodules:1-3 is absent from the clone, while action_interface.py:29 imports planner.beam_assembly and core/agent.py:12-25 imports sparc_planning and beam_assembly, none of which are in the tree. The README describes a benchmark (README.md:1-2) whose ROS device stack is cloned separately from junjungoal/franka_ros, panda_moveit_config, apriltag_ros and panda_ros_interface (README.md:28-32). There is no upstream simulator, so the card's mock_strategy 'upstream-sim' cannot be used, and the 'sim-env' role has no environment class, reset or step in the tree.

SAFETY. The interface commands a Franka arm with force-controlled insertion (tip_effort thresholds at core/action_interface.py:312, :439, :525), so the device is at least R2 even though the card floor is R1. A simulated R2 driver still needs an independent stop under the task safety rules, and the clone has none. A fake-only gate pass would therefore claim a stop the native API does not provide. No driver, fake, lock, reference or test was written, and no gate run was made. If the card is corrected to a direct-driver task with a source-backed stop from the deployed panda_interface, the route would be a direct Driver plus a native.py factory, with every unstated bound operator-required and the hardware backend unreachable until a human signs reviewed_by.

ISOLATION. The upstream clone is unchanged (git status clean at 55b2d49a1ef2e47fc92c1f1203f2212a702b9242); no upstream code was imported, installed or run, no network or pip was used, and no hardware was attached. No human review or hardware run is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the block and the card deviation after reading every cited line: the pinned tree is the RAMP assembly benchmark's baseline (README.md:1-2) for a real Franka Panda; ActionInterface only subscribes to two AprilTag topics and moves the arm through the external panda_interface PandaArmInterface (core/action_interface.py:16, 39-56), CMakeLists.txt declares no messages, services or actions, the bringup launch starts RealSense camera drivers, AprilTag detection and MoveIt (launch/bringup_interface.launch:7-31), and there is no simulator, environment class, reset, step or stop in the clone, so neither RosDriver nor a fake-only package can serve it honestly. The author's shipped-defect findings hold (main.py:13 reads assembly before assignment, pring at core/action_interface.py:320, target instead of beam at 925, the planner submodule of .gitmodules:1-3 is absent), and recover_from_errors(), called inside put_down and after insertion (657, 371), re-enables the arm rather than stopping it. Because the only path is real Franka hardware without a source-backed stop, the reviewer corrects blocked_on from HELPER_MISSING to NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH (the hardware precedent of the brief; the SDK does have a direct-Driver helper) and raises the risk to R2 (an arm with force-controlled insertion), as the author's notes already argue.
